# Week 10 assessment blueprint

This instructor-facing specification applies the LIPPS assessment standard established in Week 1. The bank contains **30 distinct scenario items** divided into 8 Practice, 16 Mastery and 6 protected Institutional seed items.

| Pool | Items | Intended use |
|---|---:|---|
| Practice | 8 | Formative learning with explanatory feedback and repeat attempts |
| Mastery | 16 | Weekly graded quiz based on application and judgement |
| Institutional | 6 | Protected seed items for later formal assessment; expand and independently review before high-stakes use |

## Recommended Moodle configuration

- **Practice:** all 8 items, untimed or generous time, immediate feedback.
- **Mastery:** randomly draw **10 of 16**, one question per page, shuffled options, pilot limit **12 minutes**.
- **Institutional:** keep hidden from routine practice; no immediate feedback; add independently reviewed parallel items before consequential use.
- Preserve approved accessibility accommodations. Timing is a secondary safeguard, never a substitute for good item design.

## Authentic task · Infodemic Signal Triage and Response Brief

**Task:** Analyse a set of information signals, distinguish misinformation and disinformation where possible, prioritise by likely health harm, and propose listening, correction, messenger and evaluation actions.

Suggested length: **900–1,200 words** or an equivalent structured product. Students should show their reasoning and identify what evidence would change their decision.

## Rubric — 20 marks

| Criterion | 4 — Excellent | 3 — Good | 2 — Developing | 1 — Weak | 0 — Missing / unsafe |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Signal interpretation** | Accurate, specific and well justified | Mostly accurate with minor gaps | Partial or generic | Weak reasoning | Missing, unsafe or unsupported |
| **Prioritisation** | Accurate, specific and well justified | Mostly accurate with minor gaps | Partial or generic | Weak reasoning | Missing, unsafe or unsupported |
| **Response design** | Accurate, specific and well justified | Mostly accurate with minor gaps | Partial or generic | Weak reasoning | Missing, unsafe or unsupported |
| **Messenger and community strategy** | Accurate, specific and well justified | Mostly accurate with minor gaps | Partial or generic | Weak reasoning | Missing, unsafe or unsupported |
| **Outcome evaluation** | Accurate, specific and well justified | Mostly accurate with minor gaps | Partial or generic | Weak reasoning | Missing, unsafe or unsupported |

**Suggested pass standard:** 10/20, subject to institutional regulation. For formal use, require minimum competence on any safety-, ethics- or evidence-critical criterion.

## Quality rule

Questions in this bank are paired around the same realistic situations: one asks the learner to **diagnose**, and the second asks the learner to **choose an action**. This deliberately tests transfer from concept to decision rather than repeated definition recall.
